Victini.description: When it shares the infinite energy it creates, that being’s entire body will be overflowing with power.

Snivy.description: They photosynthesize by bathing their tails in sunlight. When they are not feeling well, their tails droop.
Snivy.evolution: **Snivy** evolves to **Servine** starting from level 17, which evolves to **Serperior** starting from level 36.

Servine.description: When it gets dirty, its leaves can’t be used in photosynthesis, so it always keeps itself clean.
Servine.evolution: **Servine** evolves from **Snivy** starting from level 17 and evolves to **Serperior** starting from level 36.

Serperior.description: It can stop its opponents’ movements with just a glare. It takes in solar energy and boosts it internally.
Serperior.evolution: **Serperior** evolves from **Servine** starting from level 36, which evolves from **Snivy** starting from level 17.

Tepig.description: It loves to eat roasted berries, but sometimes it gets too excited and burns them to a crisp.
Tepig.evolution: **Tepig** evolves to **Pignite** starting from level 17, which evolves to **Emboar** starting from level 36.

Pignite.description: When its internal fire flares up, its movements grow sharper and faster. When in trouble, it emits smoke.
Pignite.evolution: **Pignite** evolves from **Tepig** starting from level 17 and evolves to **Emboar** starting from level 36.

Emboar.description: It has mastered fast and powerful fighting moves. It grows a beard of fire.
Emboar.evolution: **Emboar** evolves from **Pignite** starting from level 36, which evolves from **Tepig** starting from level 17.

Oshawott.description: This Pokémon from the Unova region uses the shell on its belly as a weapon to cut down its foes. Thus, I’ve conferred upon this shell the name “scalchop.”
Oshawott.evolution: **Oshawott** evolves to **Dewott** starting from level 17, which evolves to **Samurott** starting from level 36.

Dewott.description: Its exquisite double-scalchop technique is likely the result of daily training, and it can send even masters of the blade fleeing in defeat.
Dewott.evolution: **Dewott** evolves from **Oshawott** starting from level 17 and evolves to **Samurott** starting from level 36.

Samurott.description: One swing of the sword incorporated in its armor can fell an opponent. A simple glare from one of them quiets everybody.
Samurott.evolution: **Samurott** evolves from **Dewott** starting from level 36, which evolves from **Oshawott** starting from level 17.

Hisuian Samurott.description: Hard of heart and deft of blade, this rare form of Samurott is a product of the Pokémon’s evolution in the region of Hisui. Its turbulent blows crash into foes like ceaseless pounding waves.

Patrat.description: Extremely cautious, one of them will always be on the lookout, but it won’t notice a foe coming from behind.

Watchog.description: When they see an enemy, their tails stand high, and they spit the seeds of berries stored in their cheek pouches.

Lillipup.description: This Pokémon is far brighter than the average child, and Lillipup won’t forget the love it receives or any abuse it suffers.
Lillipup.evolution: **Lillipup** evolves to **Herdier** starting from level 16, which evolves to **Stoutland** starting from level 32.

Herdier.description: The black fur that covers this Pokémon’s body is dense and springy. Even sharp fangs bounce right off.
Herdier.evolution: **Herdier** evolves from **Lillipup** starting from level 16 and evolves to **Stoutland** starting from level 32.

Stoutland.description: Stoutland is immensely proud of its impressive moustache. It’s said that moustache length is what determines social standing among this species.
Stoutland.evolution: **Stoutland** evolves from **Herdier** starting from level 32, which evolves from **Lillipup** starting from level 16.

Purrloin.description: Opponents that get drawn in by its adorable behavior come away with stinging scratches from its claws and stinging pride from its laughter.

Liepard.description: This stealthy Pokémon sneaks up behind prey without making any sound at all. It competes with Thievul for territory.

Pansage.description: It’s good at finding berries and gathers them from all over. It’s kind enough to share them with friends.
Pansage.evolution: **Pansage** evolves to **Simisage** using a Leaf Stone.

Simisage.description: Ill tempered, it fights by swinging its barbed tail around wildly. The leaf growing on its head is very bitter.
Simisage.evolution: **Simisage** evolves from **Pansage** using a Leaf Stone.

Pansear.description: This Pokémon lives in caves in volcanoes. The fire within the tuft on its head can reach 600 degrees Fahrenheit.
Pansear.evolution: **Pansear** evolves to **Simisear** using a Fire Stone.

Simisear.description: When it gets excited, embers rise from its head and tail and it gets hot. For some reason, it loves sweets.
Simisear.evolution: **Simisear** evolves from **Pansear** using a Fire Stone.

Panpour.description: The water stored inside the tuft on its head is full of nutrients. Plants that receive its water grow large.
Panpour.evolution: **Panpour** evolves to **Simipour** using a Water Stone.

Simipour.description: It prefers places with clean water. When its tuft runs low, it replenishes it by siphoning up water with its tail.
Simipour.evolution: **Simipour** evolves from **Panpour** using a Water Stone.

Munna.description: It eats dreams and releases mist. The mist is pink when it’s eating a good dream, and black when it’s eating a nightmare.
Munna.evolution: **Munna** evolves to **Musharna** using a Moon Stone.

Musharna.description: It drowses and dreams all the time. It’s best to leave it be if it’s just woken up, as it’s a terrible grump when freshly roused from sleep.
Musharna.evolution: **Musharna** evolves from **Munna** using a Moon Stone.

Pidove.description: It’s forgetful and not very bright, but many Trainers love it anyway for its friendliness and sincerity.
Pidove.evolution: **Pidove** evolves to **Tranquill** starting from level 21, which evolves to **Unfezant** starting from level 32.

Tranquill.description: These bright Pokémon have acute memories. Apparently delivery workers often choose them as their partners.
Tranquill.evolution: **Tranquill** evolves from **Pidove** starting from level 21 and evolves to **Unfezant** starting from level 32.

Unfezant.description: Males have plumage on their heads. They will never let themselves feel close to anyone other than their Trainers.
Unfezant.evolution: **Unfezant** evolves from **Tranquill** starting from level 32, which evolves from **Pidove** starting from level 21.

Blitzle.description: Its mane shines when it discharges electricity. They use the frequency and rhythm of these flashes to communicate.

Zebstrika.description: They have lightning-like movements. When Zebstrika run at full speed, the sound of thunder reverberates.

Roggenrola.description: When it detects a noise, it starts to move. The energy core inside it makes this Pokémon slightly warm to the touch.
Roggenrola.evolution: **Roggenrola** evolves to **Boldore** starting from level 25, which evolves to **Gigalith** when traded.

Boldore.description: It relies on sound in order to monitor what’s in its vicinity. When angered, it will attack without ever changing the direction it’s facing.
Boldore.evolution: **Boldore** evolves from **Roggenrola** starting from level 25 and evolves to **Gigalith** when traded.

Gigalith.description: Although its energy blasts can blow away a dump truck, they have a limitation— they can only be fired when the sun is out.
Gigalith.evolution: **Gigalith** evolves from **Boldore** when traded, which evolves from **Roggenrola** starting from level 25.

Woobat.description: It emits ultrasonic waves as it flutters about, searching for its prey—bug Pokémon.
Woobat.evolution: **Woobat** evolves to **Swoobat** when leveled up while holding a Friendship Bracelet.

Swoobat.description: The auspicious shape of this Pokémon’s nose apparently led some regions to consider Swoobat a symbol of good luck.
Swoobat.evolution: **Swoobat** evolves from **Woobat** when leveled up while holding a Friendship Bracelet.

Drilbur.description: It’s a digger, using its claws to burrow through the ground. It causes damage to vegetable crops, so many farmers have little love for it.

Excadrill.description: Known as the Drill King, this Pokémon can tunnel through the terrain at speeds of over 90 mph.

Audino.description: This Pokémon has a kind heart. By touching with its feelers, Audino can gauge other creatures’ feelings and physical conditions.

Timburr.description: Timburr that have started carrying logs that are about three times their size are nearly ready to evolve.
Timburr.evolution: **Timburr** evolves to **Gurdurr** starting from level 25, which evolves to **Conkeldurr** when traded.

Gurdurr.description: Gurdurr excels at demolition—construction is not its forte. In any case, there’s skill in the way this Pokémon wields its metal beam.
Gurdurr.evolution: **Gurdurr** evolves from **Timburr** starting from level 25 and evolves to **Conkeldurr** when traded.

Conkeldurr.description: When going all out, this Pokémon throws aside its concrete pillars and leaps at opponents to pummel them with its fists.
Conkeldurr.evolution: **Conkeldurr** evolves from **Gurdurr** when traded, which evolves from **Timburr** starting from level 25.

Tympole.description: It uses sound waves to communicate with others of its kind. People and other Pokémon species can’t hear its cries of warning.
Tympole.evolution: **Tympole** evolves to **Palpitoad** starting from level 25, which evolves to **Seismitoad** starting from level 36.

Palpitoad.description: On occasion, their cries are sublimely pleasing to the ear. Palpitoad with larger lumps on their bodies can sing with a wider range of sounds.
Palpitoad.evolution: **Palpitoad** evolves from **Tympole** starting from level 25 and evolves to **Seismitoad** starting from level 36.

Seismitoad.description: This Pokémon is popular among the elderly, who say the vibrations of its lumps are great for massages.
Seismitoad.evolution: **Seismitoad** evolves from **Palpitoad** starting from level 36, which evolves from **Tympole** starting from level 25.

Throh.description: They train in groups of five. Any member that can’t keep up will discard its belt and leave the group.

Sawk.description: The karate chops of a Sawk that’s trained itself to the limit can cleave the ocean itself.

Sewaddle.description: Since this Pokémon makes its own clothes out of leaves, it is a popular mascot for fashion designers.
Sewaddle.evolution: **Sewaddle** evolves to **Swadloon** starting from level 20, which evolves to **Leavanny** when leveled up while holding a Friendship Bracelet.

Swadloon.description: It protects itself from the cold by wrapping up in leaves. It stays on the move, eating leaves in forests.
Swadloon.evolution: **Swadloon** evolves from **Sewaddle** starting from level 20 and evolves to **Leavanny** when leveled up while holding a Friendship Bracelet.

Leavanny.description: It keeps its eggs warm with heat from fermenting leaves. It also uses leaves to make warm wrappings for Sewaddle.
Leavanny.evolution: **Leavanny** evolves from **Swadloon** when leveled up while holding a Friendship Bracelet, which evolves from **Sewaddle** starting from level 20.

Venipede.description: Its fangs are highly venomous. If this Pokémon finds prey it thinks it can eat, it leaps for them without any thought of how things might turn out.
Venipede.evolution: **Venipede** evolves to **Whirlipede** starting from level 22, which evolves to **Scolipede** starting from level 30.

Whirlipede.description: Whirlipede protects itself with a sturdy shell and poisonous spikes while it stores up the energy it’ll need for evolution.
Whirlipede.evolution: **Whirlipede** evolves from **Venipede** starting from level 22 and evolves to **Scolipede** starting from level 30.

Scolipede.description: Scolipede engage in fierce territorial battles with Centiskorch. At the end of one of these battles, the victor makes a meal of the loser.
Scolipede.evolution: **Scolipede** evolves from **Whirlipede** starting from level 30, which evolves from **Venipede** starting from level 22.

Cottonee.description: Weaving together the cotton of both Cottonee and Eldegoss produces exquisite cloth that’s highly prized by many luxury brands.
Cottonee.evolution: **Cottonee** evolves to **Whimsicott** using a Sun Stone.

Whimsicott.description: As long as this Pokémon bathes in sunlight, its cotton keeps growing. If too much cotton fluff builds up, Whimsicott tears it off and scatters it.
Whimsicott.evolution: **Whimsicott** evolves from **Cottonee** using a Sun Stone.

Petilil.description: If the leaves on its head are pruned with regularity, this Pokémon can be grown into a fine plump shape.
Petilil.evolution: **Petilil** evolves to **Lilligant** using a Sun Stone.

Lilligant.description: No matter how much time and money is spent raising it, its flowers are the most beautiful when they bloom in the wild.
Lilligant.evolution: **Lilligant** evolves from **Petilil** using a Sun Stone.

Hisuian Lilligant.description: I suspect that its well-developed legs are the result of a life spent on mountains covered in deep snow. The scent it exudes from its flower crown heartens those in proximity.

Basculin.description: Red and blue Basculin usually do not get along, but sometimes members of one school mingle with the other’s school.

Blue-Striped Basculin.description: The power of its jaws is immense—enough to leave teeth marks in iron sheets. Its personality is also extremely vicious.

White-Striped Basculin.description: Though it differs from other Basculin in several respects, including demeanor—this one is gentle—I have categorized it as a regional form given the vast array of shared qualities.
White-Striped Basculin.evolution: **White-Striped Basculin** evolves to **Basculegion** starting from level 29.

Sandile.description: They live hidden under hot desert sands in order to keep their body temperature from dropping.
Sandile.evolution: **Sandile** evolves to **Krokorok** starting from level 29, which evolves to **Krookodile** starting from level 40.

Krokorok.description: Thanks to the special membrane covering its eyes, it can see its surroundings clearly, even in the middle of the night.
Krokorok.evolution: **Krokorok** evolves from **Sandile** starting from level 29 and evolves to **Krookodile** starting from level 40.

Krookodile.description: Its unique faculty of sight can detect small prey more than 30 miles away, even in the midst of a sandstorm.
Krookodile.evolution: **Krookodile** evolves from **Krokorok** starting from level 40, which evolves from **Sandile** starting from level 29.

Darumaka.description: This popular symbol of good fortune will never fall over in its sleep, no matter how it’s pushed or pulled.

Galarian Darumaka.description: The colder they get, the more energetic they are. They freeze their breath to make snowballs, using them as ammo for playful snowball fights.
Galarian Darumaka.evolution: **Galarian Darumaka** evolves to **Galarian Darmanitan** using a Ice Stone.

Darmanitan.description: Its internal fire burns at 2,500 degrees Fahrenheit, making enough power that it can destroy a dump truck with one punch.

Zen Darmanitan.description: When wounded, it stops moving. It goes as still as stone to meditate, sharpening its mind and spirit.
Zen Darmanitan.evolution: **Zen Darmanitan** transforms from **Darmanitan** when given a Transformation.

Galarian Darmanitan.description: Though it has a gentle disposition, it’s also very strong. It will quickly freeze the snowball on its head before going for a headbutt.
Galarian Darmanitan.evolution: **Galarian Darmanitan** evolves from **Galarian Darumaka** using a Ice Stone.

Galarian Zen Darmanitan.description: Darmanitan takes this form when enraged. It won’t stop spewing flames until its rage has settled, even if its body starts to melt.

Maractus.description: Once each year, this Pokémon scatters its seeds. They’re jam-packed with nutrients, making them a precious food source out in the desert.

Dwebble.description: It first tries to find a rock to live in, but if there are no suitable rocks to be found, Dwebble may move in to the ports of a Hippowdon.

Crustle.description: Its thick claws are its greatest weapons. They’re mighty enough to crack Rhyperior’s carapace.

Scraggy.description: It protects itself with its durable skin. It’s thought that this Pokémon will evolve once its skin has completely stretched out.

Scrafty.description: While mostly known for having the temperament of an aggressive ruffian, this Pokémon takes very good care of its family, friends, and territory.

Sigilyph.description: A discovery was made in the desert where Sigilyph fly. The ruins of what may have been an ancient city were found beneath the sands.

Yamask.description: The spirit of a person from a bygone age became this Pokémon. It rambles through ruins, searching for someone who knows its face.

Galarian Yamask.description: It’s said that this Pokémon was formed when an ancient clay tablet was drawn to a vengeful spirit.

Cofagrigus.description: There are many depictions of Cofagrigus decorating ancient tombs. They’re symbols of the wealth that kings of bygone eras had.

Tirtouga.description: Tirtouga is considered to be the ancestor of many turtle Pokémon. It was restored to life from a fossil.

Carracosta.description: This Pokémon emerges from the water in search of prey despite the fact that it moves more slowly on land.

Archen.description: Archen is said to be the ancestor of bird Pokémon. It lived in treetops, eating berries and bug Pokémon.

Archeops.description: Though capable of flight, Archeops was apparently better at hunting on the ground.

Trubbish.description: This Pokémon was born from a bag stuffed with trash. Galarian Weezing relish the fumes belched by Trubbish.

Garbodor.description: The toxic liquid it launches from its right arm is so virulent that it can kill a weakened creature instantly.

Zorua.description: To protect themselves from danger, they hide their true identities by transforming into people and Pokémon.

Hisuian Zorua.description: A once-departed soul, returned to life in Hisui. Derives power from resentment, which rises as energy atop its head and takes on the forms of foes. In this way, Zorua vents lingering malice.
Hisuian Zorua.evolution: **Hisuian Zorua** evolves to **Hisuian Zoroark** starting from level 30.

Zoroark.description: Each has the ability to fool a large group of people simultaneously. They protect their lair with illusory scenery.

Hisuian Zoroark.description: With its disheveled white fur, it looks like an embodiment of death. Heedless of its own safety, Zoroark attacks its nemeses with a bitter energy so intense, it lacerates Zoroark’s own body.
Hisuian Zoroark.evolution: **Hisuian Zoroark** evolves from **Hisuian Zorua** starting from level 30.

Minccino.description: They pet each other with their tails as a form of greeting. Of the two, the one whose tail is fluffier is a bit more boastful.
Minccino.evolution: **Minccino** evolves to **Cinccino** using a Shiny Stone.

Cinccino.description: A special oil that seeps through their fur helps them avoid attacks. The oil fetches a high price at market.
Cinccino.evolution: **Cinccino** evolves from **Minccino** using a Shiny Stone.

Gothita.description: Beware of touching the ribbon-shaped feelers that control its psychic power. Gothita will begin bawling if you do.
Gothita.evolution: **Gothita** evolves to **Gothorita** starting from level 32, which evolves to **Gothitelle** starting from level 41.

Gothorita.description: Using its psychic power, it arranges pebbles to form the shapes of constellations. Some people believe this Pokémon came from outer space.
Gothorita.evolution: **Gothorita** evolves from **Gothita** starting from level 32 and evolves to **Gothitelle** starting from level 41.

Gothitelle.description: It gazes at the stars to predict the future. It acts somewhat detached because it has seen the end of all existence.
Gothitelle.evolution: **Gothitelle** evolves from **Gothorita** starting from level 41, which evolves from **Gothita** starting from level 32.

Solosis.description: Many say that the special liquid covering this Pokémon’s body would allow it to survive in the vacuum of space.
Solosis.evolution: **Solosis** evolves to **Duosion** starting from level 32, which evolves to **Reuniclus** starting from level 41.

Duosion.description: Its brain has split into two, and the two halves rarely think alike. Its actions are utterly unpredictable.
Duosion.evolution: **Duosion** evolves from **Solosis** starting from level 32 and evolves to **Reuniclus** starting from level 41.

Reuniclus.description: It’s said that drinking the liquid surrounding Reuniclus grants wisdom. Problem is, the liquid is highly toxic to anything besides Reuniclus itself.
Reuniclus.evolution: **Reuniclus** evolves from **Duosion** starting from level 41, which evolves from **Solosis** starting from level 32.

Ducklett.description: They are better at swimming than flying, and they happily eat their favorite food, peat moss, as they dive underwater.

Swanna.description: Swanna start to dance at dusk. The one dancing in the middle is the leader of the flock.

Vanillite.description: Supposedly, this Pokémon was born from an icicle. It spews out freezing air at −58 degrees Fahrenheit to make itself more comfortable.
Vanillite.evolution: **Vanillite** evolves to **Vanillish** starting from level 35, which evolves to **Vanilluxe** starting from level 47.

Vanillish.description: It blasts enemies with cold air reaching −148 degrees Fahrenheit, freezing them solid. But it spares their lives afterward—it’s a kind Pokémon.
Vanillish.evolution: **Vanillish** evolves from **Vanillite** starting from level 35 and evolves to **Vanilluxe** starting from level 47.

Vanilluxe.description: People believe this Pokémon formed when two Vanillish stuck together. Its body temperature is roughly 21 degrees Fahrenheit.
Vanilluxe.evolution: **Vanilluxe** evolves from **Vanillish** starting from level 47, which evolves from **Vanillite** starting from level 35.

Deerling.description: The turning of the seasons changes the color and scent of this Pokémon’s fur. People use it to mark the seasons.

Summer Deerling.description: Deerling have different scents depending on the season. When a distinct grassy smell starts to waft from one, you know that summer has begun.
Summer Deerling.evolution: **Summer Deerling** evolves to **Summer Sawsbuck** starting from level 34.

Autumn Deerling.description: Deerling have different scents depending on the season. In this form, Deerling have a softly sweet scent that lingers in the nose.
Autumn Deerling.evolution: **Autumn Deerling** evolves to **Autumn Sawsbuck** starting from level 34.

Winter Deerling.description: This Pokémon will playfully headbutt those it gets along well with. It has antlers hidden under its flower, so the headbutts are a little painful.
Winter Deerling.evolution: **Winter Deerling** evolves to **Winter Sawsbuck** starting from level 34.

Sawsbuck.description: They migrate according to the seasons, so some people call Sawsbuck the harbingers of spring.

Summer Sawsbuck.description: This Pokémon's leaves can be made into a black tea, the taste of which varies depending on the region of origin. Paldea's is especially aromatic.
Summer Sawsbuck.evolution: **Summer Sawsbuck** evolves from **Summer Deerling** starting from level 34.

Autumn Sawsbuck.description: Sawsbuck in their Autumn Form are known for having very short tempers. The males fight each other incessantly.
Autumn Sawsbuck.evolution: **Autumn Sawsbuck** evolves from **Autumn Deerling** starting from level 34.

Winter Sawsbuck.description: Though there are many enthusiasts for Sawsbuck as a species, this seasonal form in particular is not very popular.
Winter Sawsbuck.evolution: **Winter Sawsbuck** evolves from **Winter Deerling** starting from level 34.

Emolga.description: This Pokémon absolutely loves sweet berries. Sometimes it stuffs its cheeks full of so much food that it can’t fly properly.

Karrablast.description: It spits a liquid from its mouth to melt through Shelmet’s shell. Karrablast doesn’t eat the shell— it eats only the contents.
Karrablast.evolution: **Karrablast** evolves to **Escavalier** when traded for a Shelmet.

Escavalier.description: It charges its enemies, lances at the ready. An image of one of its duels is captured in a famous painting of Escavalier clashing with Sirfetch’d.
Escavalier.evolution: **Escavalier** evolves from **Karrablast** when traded for a Shelmet.

Foongus.description: This Pokémon prefers damp places. It spurts out poison spores to repel approaching enemies.

Amoonguss.description: Amoonguss mimics Poké Balls. It is not yet clear whether this mimicry is effective against other Pokémon.

Frillish.description: Using the invisible poison spikes on its veillike arms and legs, it paralyzes its enemies and causes them to drown.

Jellicent.description: Fishermen are terrified of Jellicent. It’s rumored to drag them into the sea and steal their lives away.

Alomomola.description: They float upon the open sea. Many water Pokémon gather in the area around Alomomola.

Joltik.description: Joltik latch on to other Pokémon and suck out static electricity. They’re often found sticking to Yamper’s hindquarters.

Galvantula.description: It lays traps of electrified threads near the nests of bird Pokémon, aiming to snare chicks that are not yet good at flying.

Ferroseed.description: Mossy caves are their preferred dwellings. Enzymes contained in mosses help Ferroseed’s spikes grow big and strong.

Ferrothorn.description: Its spikes are harder than steel. This Pokémon crawls across rock walls by stabbing the spikes on its feelers into the stone.

Klink.description: It’s suspected that Klink were the inspiration behind ancient people’s invention of the first gears.
Klink.evolution: **Klink** evolves to **Klang** starting from level 38, which evolves to **Klinklang** starting from level 49.

Klang.description: Many companies in the Galar region choose Klang as their logo. This Pokémon is considered the symbol of industrial technology.
Klang.evolution: **Klang** evolves from **Klink** starting from level 38 and evolves to **Klinklang** starting from level 49.

Klinklang.description: The three gears that compose this Pokémon spin at high speed. Its new spiked gear isn’t a living creature.
Klinklang.evolution: **Klinklang** evolves from **Klang** starting from level 49, which evolves from **Klink** starting from level 38.

Tynamo.description: These Pokémon move in schools. They have an electricity-generating organ, so they discharge electricity if in danger.
Tynamo.evolution: **Tynamo** evolves to **Eelektrik** starting from level 39, which evolves to **Eelektross** using a Thunder Stone.

Eelektrik.description: These Pokémon have a big appetite. When they spot their prey, they attack it and paralyze it with electricity.
Eelektrik.evolution: **Eelektrik** evolves from **Tynamo** starting from level 39 and evolves to **Eelektross** using a Thunder Stone.

Eelektross.description: It latches on to prey with its sucker mouth, sinking in its fangs and shocking the prey with powerful electricity.
Eelektross.evolution: **Eelektross** evolves from **Eelektrik** using a Thunder Stone, which evolves from **Tynamo** starting from level 39.

Elgyem.description: This Pokémon was discovered about 50 years ago. Its highly developed brain enables it to exert its psychic powers.

Beheeyem.description: Sometimes found drifting above wheat fields, this Pokémon can control the memories of its opponents.

Litwick.description: The younger the life this Pokémon absorbs, the brighter and eerier the flame on its head burns.
Litwick.evolution: **Litwick** evolves to **Lampent** starting from level 41, which evolves to **Chandelure** using a Dusk Stone.

Lampent.description: It lurks in cities, pretending to be a lamp. Once it finds someone whose death is near, it will trail quietly after them.
Lampent.evolution: **Lampent** evolves from **Litwick** starting from level 41 and evolves to **Chandelure** using a Dusk Stone.

Chandelure.description: In homes illuminated by Chandelure instead of lights, funerals were a constant occurrence— or so it’s said.
Chandelure.evolution: **Chandelure** evolves from **Lampent** using a Dusk Stone, which evolves from **Litwick** starting from level 41.

Axew.description: If you see peculiar teeth marks on boulders or trees, it means an Axew is likely living nearby.
Axew.evolution: **Axew** evolves to **Fraxure** starting from level 38, which evolves to **Haxorus** starting from level 48.

Fraxure.description: Fraxure uses its thick tusks to neatly cut prey into two portions—one to eat now and one to save for later.
Fraxure.evolution: **Fraxure** evolves from **Axew** starting from level 38 and evolves to **Haxorus** starting from level 48.

Haxorus.description: It overwhelms enemies with its prized tusks, which are sharp enough to cut through a metal transmission tower in one strike.
Haxorus.evolution: **Haxorus** evolves from **Fraxure** starting from level 48, which evolves from **Axew** starting from level 38.

Cubchoo.description: When Cubchoo starts sneezing, watch out! If it spatters you with its frosty snot, you’ll get frostbite.

Beartic.description: Feared as the Snow-White Demon in northern lands, Beartic uses its frosty claws and fangs to attack prey.

Cryogonal.description: Cryogonal uses its chains of ice to constrict its opponents and then flash-freezes them where they stand.

Shelmet.description: It has a strange physiology that responds to electricity. When together with Karrablast, Shelmet evolves for some reason.
Shelmet.evolution: **Shelmet** evolves to **Accelgor** when traded for a Karrablast.

Accelgor.description: Discarding its shell made it nimble. To keep itself from dehydrating, it wraps its body in bands of membrane.
Accelgor.evolution: **Accelgor** evolves from **Shelmet** when traded for a Karrablast.

Stunfisk.description: For some reason, this Pokémon smiles slightly when it emits a strong electric current from the yellow markings on its body.

Galarian Stunfisk.description: Its conspicuous lips lure prey in as it lies in wait in the mud. When prey gets close, Stunfisk clamps its jagged steel fins down on them.

Mienfoo.description: Though small, Mienfoo’s temperament is fierce. Any creature that approaches Mienfoo carelessly will be greeted with a flurry of graceful attacks.

Mienshao.description: Delivered at blinding speeds, kicks from this Pokémon can shatter massive boulders into tiny pieces.

Druddigon.description: Druddigon are vicious and cunning. They take up residence in nests dug out by other Pokémon, treating the stolen nests as their own lairs.

Golett.description: This Pokémon was created from clay. It received orders from its master many thousands of years ago, and it still follows those orders to this day.

Golurk.description: There’s a theory that inside Golurk is a perpetual motion machine that produces limitless energy, but this belief hasn’t been proven.

Pawniard.description: Any chips in its blades would prove fatal for it. After each battle, it diligently maintains its blades using its favorite sharpening stone.
Pawniard.evolution: **Pawniard** evolves to **Bisharp** starting from level 52, which evolves to **Kingambit** when leveled up while holding a Leader's Crest.

Bisharp.description: Bisharp mercilessly cuts its opponents to pieces with the sharp blades covering its body. It will do anything to win.
Bisharp.evolution: **Bisharp** evolves from **Pawniard** starting from level 52 and evolves to **Kingambit** when leveled up while holding a Leader's Crest.

Bouffalant.description: These Pokémon live in herds of about 20 individuals. Bouffalant that betray the herd will lose the hair on their heads for some reason.

Rufflet.description: With its sharp claws, this Pokémon pierces its prey, and then it pecks at them. Although it also consumes berries, it’s a carnivore at heart.

Braviary.description: For the sake of its friends, this brave warrior of the sky will not stop battling, even if injured.

Hisuian Braviary.description: Screaming a bloodcurdling battle cry, this huge and ferocious bird Pokémon goes out on the hunt. It blasts lakes with shock waves, then scoops up any prey that float to the water’s surface.

Vullaby.description: Vullaby grow quickly. Bones that have gotten too small for older Vullaby to wear often get passed down to younger ones in the nest.

Mandibuzz.description: They adorn themselves with bones. There seem to be fashion trends among them, as different bones come into and fall out of popularity.

Heatmor.description: A flame serves as its tongue, melting through the hard shell of Durant so that Heatmor can devour their insides.

Durant.description: With their large mandibles, these Pokémon can crunch their way through rock. They work together to protect their eggs from Sandaconda.

Deino.description: It nests deep inside a cave. Food there is scarce, so Deino will sink its teeth into anything that moves and attempt to eat it.
Deino.evolution: **Deino** evolves to **Zweilous** starting from level 50, which evolves to **Hydreigon** starting from level 64.

Zweilous.description: The two heads have different likes and dislikes. Because the heads fight with each other, Zweilous gets stronger without needing to rely on others.
Zweilous.evolution: **Zweilous** evolves from **Deino** starting from level 50 and evolves to **Hydreigon** starting from level 64.

Hydreigon.description: It’s said that Hydreigon grew ferocious because people in times long past loathed it, considering it to be evil incarnate and attacking it relentlessly.
Hydreigon.evolution: **Hydreigon** evolves from **Zweilous** starting from level 64, which evolves from **Deino** starting from level 50.

Larvesta.description: In ancient times, Larvesta was worshiped as the emissary of the sun. However, it was also viewed as a burden since it often caused forest fires.

Volcarona.description: This Pokémon scatters burning scales. Most of the danger of these scales is not in their heat—it’s in the way they rob the surrounding air of oxygen.

Cobalion.description: From the moment it’s born, this Pokémon radiates the air of a leader. Its presence will calm even vicious foes.

Terrakion.description: In Unovan legend, Terrakion battled against humans in an effort to protect other Pokémon.

Virizion.description: It darts around opponents with a flurry of quick movements, slicing them up with its horns.

Tornadus.description: This storm-stirring Pokémon is said to cause the seasons to turn by whipping up the air. I suspect its humanlike form to be a false one.

Thundurus.description: They say this wielder of electricity has waged war with its nemesis, Tornadus, since time immemorial. The lightning bolts it hurls pierce the very earth and enrich the soil.

Reshiram.description: According to myth, if people ignore truth and let themselves become consumed by greed, Reshiram will arrive to burn their kingdoms down.

Zekrom.description: Mythology tells us that if people lose the righteousness in their hearts, their kingdoms will be razed by Zekrom’s lightning.

Landorus.description: When the incarnations of wind and of lightning clash, Landorus arrives to quell the conflict. After the tempests and thunderbolts abate, the land is sure to be blessed with bountiful harvests.

Kyurem.description: It appears that this Pokémon uses its powers over ice to freeze its own body in order to stabilize its cellular structure.

Keldeo.description: When it is resolute, its body fills with power and it becomes swifter. Its jumps are then too fast to follow.
Keldeo.evolution: **Keldeo** transforms to **Resolute Keldeo** when leveled up while knowing Secret Sword.

Meloetta.description: Its melodies are sung with a special vocalization method that can control the feelings of those who hear it.
Meloetta.evolution: **Meloetta** transforms to **Pirouette Meloetta** when leveled up while knowing Relic Song.

Pirouette Meloetta.evolution: **Pirouette Meloetta** transforms from **Meloetta** when leveled up while knowing Relic Song.

Genesect.description: This Pokémon existed 300 million years ago. Team Plasma altered it and attached a cannon to its back.

High-speed Flight Configuration Genesect.evolution: **High-speed Flight Configuration Genesect** transforms from **Genesect** when given a Transformation.

Chespin.description: Such a thick shell of wood covers its head and back that even a direct hit from a truck wouldn’t faze it.
Chespin.evolution: **Chespin** evolves to **Quilladin** starting from level 16, which evolves to **Chesnaught** starting from level 36.

Quilladin.description: They strengthen their lower bodies by running into one another. They are very kind and won’t start fights.
Quilladin.evolution: **Quilladin** evolves from **Chespin** starting from level 16 and evolves to **Chesnaught** starting from level 36.

Chesnaught.description: When it takes a defensive posture with its fists guarding its face, it could withstand a bomb blast.

Fennekin.evolution: **Fennekin** evolves to **Braixen** starting from level 16, which evolves to **Delphox** starting from level 36.

Braixen.evolution: **Braixen** evolves from **Fennekin** starting from level 16 and evolves to **Delphox** starting from level 36.

Delphox.evolution: **Delphox** evolves from **Braixen** starting from level 36, which evolves from **Fennekin** starting from level 16.

Froakie.evolution: **Froakie** evolves to **Frogadier** starting from level 16, which evolves to **Greninja** starting from level 36.

Frogadier.evolution: **Frogadier** evolves from **Froakie** starting from level 16 and evolves to **Greninja** starting from level 36.

Diggersby.description: The fur on its belly retains heat exceptionally well. People used to make heavy winter clothing from fur shed by this Pokémon.

Fletchling.description: Fletchling can be found in both rural and urban areas. They once had a huge territorial dispute with Squawkabilly. Fights broke out all over town.
Fletchling.evolution: **Fletchling** evolves to **Fletchinder** starting from level 17, which evolves to **Talonflame** starting from level 35.

Fletchinder.evolution: **Fletchinder** evolves from **Fletchling** starting from level 17 and evolves to **Talonflame** starting from level 35.

Gogoat.description: These Pokémon live in herds in mountainous places. The victor in their contests of clashing horns will become the leader of the herd.

Pancham.description: Wanting to make sure it’s taken seriously, Pancham’s always giving others a glare. But if it’s not focusing, it ends up smiling.

Pangoro.description: Using its leaf, Pangoro can predict the moves of its opponents. It strikes with punches that can turn a dump truck into scrap with just one hit.

Pharaoh Trim Furfrou.description: Left alone, its fur will grow longer and longer, but it will only allow someone it trusts to cut it.
Pharaoh Trim Furfrou.evolution: **Pharaoh Trim Furfrou** transforms from **Furfrou** when given a Shears.

Espurr.description: There’s enough psychic power in Espurr to send a wrestler flying, but because this power can’t be controlled, Espurr finds it troublesome.

Meowstic.description: The eyeball patterns on the interior of its ears emit psychic energy. It keeps the patterns tightly covered because that power is too immense.

Honedge.description: The blue eye on the sword’s handguard is the true body of Honedge. With its old cloth, it drains people’s lives away.
Honedge.evolution: **Honedge** evolves to **Doublade** starting from level 35, which evolves to **Aegislash** using a Dusk Stone.

Doublade.description: The two swords employ a strategy of rapidly alternating between offense and defense to bring down their prey.
Doublade.evolution: **Doublade** evolves from **Honedge** starting from level 35 and evolves to **Aegislash** using a Dusk Stone.

Aegislash.description: Apparently, it can detect the innate qualities of leadership. According to legend, whoever it recognizes is destined to become king.
Aegislash.evolution: **Aegislash** evolves from **Doublade** using a Dusk Stone, which evolves from **Honedge** starting from level 35.

Blade Aegislash.description: Once upon a time, a king with an Aegislash reigned over the land. His Pokémon eventually drained him of life, and his kingdom fell with him.
Blade Aegislash.evolution: **Blade Aegislash** transforms from **Aegislash** when given a Transformation.

Spritzee.description: The scent its body gives off enraptures those who smell it. Noble ladies had no shortage of love for Spritzee.
Spritzee.evolution: **Spritzee** evolves to **Aromatisse** when traded while holding a Sachet.

Aromatisse.description: The scents Aromatisse can produce range from sweet smells that bolster allies to foul smells that sap an opponent’s will to fight.
Aromatisse.evolution: **Aromatisse** evolves from **Spritzee** when traded while holding a Sachet.

Swirlix.description: The sweet smell of cotton candy perfumes Swirlix’s fluffy fur. This Pokémon spits out sticky string to tangle up its enemies.
Swirlix.evolution: **Swirlix** evolves to **Slurpuff** when traded while holding a Whipped Dream.

Slurpuff.description: Slurpuff’s fur contains a lot of air, making it soft to the touch and lighter than it looks.
Slurpuff.evolution: **Slurpuff** evolves from **Swirlix** when traded while holding a Whipped Dream.

Inkay.description: By exposing foes to the blinking of its luminescent spots, Inkay demoralizes them, and then it seizes the chance to flee.

Malamar.description: It’s said that Malamar’s hypnotic powers played a role in certain history-changing events.

Binacle.description: If the two don’t work well together, both their offense and defense fall apart. Without good teamwork, they won’t survive.

Barbaracle.description: Having an eye on each palm allows it to keep watch in all directions. In a pinch, its limbs start to act on their own to ensure the enemy’s defeat.

Skrelp.description: This Pokémon is a poor swimmer. If it’s caught in a fierce storm, it will sometimes get washed far away and become unable to return to its home.

Dragalge.description: Since Finizen is the better swimmer, Dragalge will approach it under the cover of seaweed, then immobilize it with a poisonous attack.

Clauncher.description: Clauncher’s claws will regrow if they fall off. The meat inside the claws is edible, but it has a distinct flavor that doesn’t appeal to all tastes.

Clawitzer.description: The cannonballs of seawater that Clawitzer launches from its claw are powerful enough to punch through tanker hulls.

Helioptile.description: The sun powers this Pokémon’s electricity generation. Interruption of that process stresses Helioptile to the point of weakness.
Helioptile.evolution: **Helioptile** evolves to **Heliolisk** using a Sun Stone.

Heliolisk.description: One Heliolisk basking in the sun with its frill outspread is all it would take to produce enough electricity to power a city.
Heliolisk.evolution: **Heliolisk** evolves from **Helioptile** using a Sun Stone.

Tyrunt.description: This Pokémon is selfish and likes to be pampered. It can also inflict grievous wounds on its Trainer just by playing around.
Tyrunt.evolution: **Tyrunt** evolves to **Tyrantrum** starting from level 39 in the daytime.

Tyrantrum.description: A single bite of Tyrantrum’s massive jaws will demolish a car. This Pokémon was the king of the ancient world.
Tyrantrum.evolution: **Tyrantrum** evolves from **Tyrunt** starting from level 39 in the daytime.

Amaura.description: Amaura is an ancient Pokémon that has gone extinct. Specimens of this species can sometimes be found frozen in ice.
Amaura.evolution: **Amaura** evolves to **Aurorus** starting from level 39 in the nighttime.

Aurorus.description: When gripped by rage, Aurorus will emanate freezing air, covering everything around it in ice.
Aurorus.evolution: **Aurorus** evolves from **Amaura** starting from level 39 in the nighttime.

Sylveon.description: Sylveon cuts an elegant figure as it dances lightly around, feelers fluttering, but its piercing moves aim straight for its opponents’ weak spots.
Sylveon.evolution: **Sylveon** evolves from **Eevee** when leveled up while knowing a Fairy-type move.

Hawlucha.description: Hawlucha live quietly without flocking together. They fight constantly with their natural enemies: noisy groups of Primeape.

Dedenne.description: Dedenne emit electrical waves from the whiskers on their cheeks to communicate with each other. When low on electricity, they curl up and sleep.

Carbink.description: It’s said that somewhere in the world, there’s a mineral vein housing a large pack of slumbering Carbink. It’s also said that this pack has a queen.

Goomy.description: Goomy’s horns are excellent sensory organs that cover all five of Goomy’s senses. Goomy picks up on danger from the movement of the air.
Goomy.evolution: **Goomy** evolves to **Sliggoo** starting from level 40, which evolves to **Goodra** starting from level 50.

Sliggoo.description: When Sliggoo senses danger, the mucus coating its entire body becomes more concentrated—it’ll dissolve anything.
Sliggoo.evolution: **Sliggoo** evolves from **Goomy** starting from level 40 and evolves to **Goodra** starting from level 50.

Hisuian Sliggoo.description: A creature given to melancholy. I suspect its metallic shell developed as a result of the mucus on its skin reacting with the iron in Hisui’s water.
Hisuian Sliggoo.evolution: **Hisuian Sliggoo** evolves to **Hisuian Goodra** starting from level 50.

Goodra.description: This Pokémon is uncontrollable when enraged. It rampages on and on, lashing its tail with enough power to send a dump truck flying.
Goodra.evolution: **Goodra** evolves from **Sliggoo** starting from level 50, which evolves from **Goomy** starting from level 40.

Hisuian Goodra.description: Able to freely control the hardness of its metallic shell. It loathes solitude and is extremely clingy—it will fume and run riot if those dearest to it ever leave its side.
Hisuian Goodra.evolution: **Hisuian Goodra** evolves from **Hisuian Sliggoo** starting from level 50.

Klefki.description: In the past, noble families entrusted their vault keys to a Klefki. They passed the Klefki down through the generations, taking good care of it.

Phantump.description: With a voice like a human child’s, it cries out to lure adults deep into the forest, getting them lost among the trees.

Trevenant.description: Small roots that extend from the tips of this Pokémon’s feet can tie into the trees of the forest and give Trevenant control over them.

Pumpkaboo.description: It is said to carry wandering spirits to the place where they belong so they can move on.

Gourgeist.description: It enwraps its prey in its hairlike arms. It sings joyfully as it observes the suffering of its prey.

Bergmite.description: Bergmite protects itself by coating its body in ice formed by frigid air of −148 degrees Fahrenheit. It fights with Frigibax whenever they meet.

Avalugg.description: This Pokémon uses its massive icy body to flatten anything that gets in its way. When it’s floating out on the ocean, it looks exactly like drift ice.

Hisuian Avalugg.description: The armor of ice covering its lower jaw puts steel to shame and can shatter rocks with ease. This Pokémon barrels along steep mountain paths, cleaving through the deep snow.

Noibat.description: Noibat can change the frequency of its sound waves at will, and it generates ultrasonic waves of up to 200,000 hertz.

Noivern.description: In the dark, even Hydreigon are terrified of this Pokémon. But in the light, Noivern is the one that avoids battle.

Xerneas.description: When the horns on its head shine in seven colors, it is said to be sharing everlasting life.

Neutral Xerneas.evolution: **Neutral Xerneas** transforms from **Xerneas** when given a Transformation.

Yveltal.description: When its life comes to an end, it absorbs the life energy of every living thing and turns into a cocoon once more.

Zygarde.description: Some say it can change to an even more powerful form when battling those who threaten the ecosystem.

10% Zygarde.description: Born when around 10% of Zygarde’s cells have been gathered from all over, this form is skilled in close-range combat.

Complete Zygarde.description: Born when all of Zygarde’s cells have been gathered together, it uses force to neutralize those who harm the ecosystem.
names: 🇯🇵 パーフェクトフォルム

Zygarde Cell.description: The Zygarde Cells form the rest of Zygarde's body and are only able to act on the Core's orders. The Zygarde Cells allows the Zygarde Core to observe the ecosystem, allowing them to see through their eyes.

Zygarde Core.description: The Zygarde Core remains in watch of the region, usually living in caves. The Cores have their own will and are sometimes able to act on their own. The Zygarde Core can order Zygarde Cells, commanding them to fly towards it to form Zygarde's body in order to protect the ecosystem.

Diancie.description: It can instantly create many diamonds by compressing the carbon in the air between its hands.

Hoopa.description: It is said to be able to seize anything it desires with its six rings and six huge arms. With its power sealed, it is transformed into a much smaller form.

Volcanion.description: It expels its internal steam from the arms on its back. It has enough power to blow away a mountain.

Rowlet.description: Flies noiselessly on delicate wings. It has mastered the art of deftly launching dagger-sharp feathers from those same wings.
Rowlet.evolution: **Rowlet** evolves to **Dartrix** starting from level 17, which evolves to **Decidueye** starting from level 34.

Dartrix.description: Regularly basks in sunlight to gather power—presumably due to the frigid climate. Nonetheless, the edges of the blade quills set into its wings are keen as ever.
Dartrix.evolution: **Dartrix** evolves from **Rowlet** starting from level 17 and evolves to **Decidueye** starting from level 34.

Decidueye.description: In a tenth of a second, it can nock and fire an arrow quill, piercing an opponent’s weak point before they notice what’s happening.
Decidueye.evolution: **Decidueye** evolves from **Dartrix** starting from level 34, which evolves from **Rowlet** starting from level 17.

Hisuian Decidueye.description: The air stored inside the rachises of Decidueye’s feathers insulates the Pokémon against Hisui’s extreme cold. This is firm proof that evolution can be influenced by environment.

Litten.description: Trying to pet Litten before it trusts you will result in a nasty scratch from its sharp claws. Be careful.
Litten.evolution: **Litten** evolves to **Torracat** starting from level 17, which evolves to **Incineroar** starting from level 34.

Torracat.description: When facing a powerful enemy, Torracat’s fighting spirit gets pumped up, and its fire bell blazes hotter.
Torracat.evolution: **Torracat** evolves from **Litten** starting from level 17 and evolves to **Incineroar** starting from level 34.

Incineroar.description: Incineroar’s rough and aggressive behavior is its most notable trait, but the way it helps out small Pokémon shows that it has a kind side as well.
Incineroar.evolution: **Incineroar** evolves from **Torracat** starting from level 34, which evolves from **Litten** starting from level 17.

Popplio.description: If Popplio want to create big, powerful balloons, they must be persistent. It takes daily practice for these Pokémon to develop their skills.
Popplio.evolution: **Popplio** evolves to **Brionne** starting from level 17, which evolves to **Primarina** starting from level 34.

Brionne.description: On nights when the sea is calm, Brionne dance with one another to the singing of the Primarina that’s leading them.
Brionne.evolution: **Brionne** evolves from **Popplio** starting from level 17 and evolves to **Primarina** starting from level 34.

Primarina.description: For Primarina, every battle’s a stage. Its singing and the dancing of its balloons will mesmerize the audience.
Primarina.evolution: **Primarina** evolves from **Brionne** starting from level 34, which evolves from **Popplio** starting from level 17.

Pikipek.description: It may look spindly, but its neck muscles are heavy-duty. It can peck at a tree 16 times per second!
Pikipek.evolution: **Pikipek** evolves to **Trumbeak** starting from level 14, which evolves to **Toucannon** starting from level 28.

Trumbeak.description: From its mouth, it fires the seeds of berries it has eaten. The scattered seeds give rise to new plants.
Trumbeak.evolution: **Trumbeak** evolves from **Pikipek** starting from level 14 and evolves to **Toucannon** starting from level 28.

Toucannon.description: Known for forming harmonious couples, this Pokémon is brought to wedding ceremonies as a good luck charm.
Toucannon.evolution: **Toucannon** evolves from **Trumbeak** starting from level 28, which evolves from **Pikipek** starting from level 14.

Yungoos.description: It spends its waking hours searching endlessly for food. When Yungoos is hungry, its ferocity gains a certain edge.
Yungoos.evolution: **Yungoos** evolves to **Gumshoos** starting from level 20 in the daytime.

Gumshoos.description: Gumshoos specializes in relentlessly tracking down prey. The simple-minded Skwovet doesn’t seem to provide Gumshoos enough challenge.
Gumshoos.evolution: **Gumshoos** evolves from **Yungoos** starting from level 20 in the daytime.

Grubbin.description: It uses its big jaws to dig nests into the forest floor, and it loves to feed on sweet tree sap.
Grubbin.evolution: **Grubbin** evolves to **Charjabug** starting from level 20, which evolves to **Vikavolt** when leveled up.

Charjabug.description: Its digestive processes convert the leaves it eats into electricity. An electric sac in its belly stores the electricity for later use.
Charjabug.evolution: **Charjabug** evolves from **Grubbin** starting from level 20 and evolves to **Vikavolt** when leveled up.

Vikavolt.description: If it carries a Charjabug to use as a spare battery, a flying Vikavolt can rapidly fire high-powered beams of electricity.
Vikavolt.evolution: **Vikavolt** evolves from **Charjabug** when leveled up, which evolves from **Grubbin** starting from level 20.

Crabrawler.description: If it loses its pincers, they’ll quickly regrow. The pincers are popular ingredients in paella since their shells produce a tasty soup stock.
Crabrawler.evolution: **Crabrawler** evolves to **Crabominable** using a Ice Stone.

Crabominable.description: Though its punches are powerful, this Pokémon’s movements are sluggish. It blows icy bubbles from its mouth to immobilize its opponents.
Crabominable.evolution: **Crabominable** evolves from **Crabrawler** using a Ice Stone.

Oricorio.description: This form of Oricorio has sipped red nectar. It whips up blazing flames as it moves to the steps of its passionate dance.

Pom-pom Oricorio.description: The energetic, cheerful dance of these Oricorio is popular with children, but the Oricorio themselves are hard to find in Paldea.
Pom-pom Oricorio.evolution: **Pom-pom Oricorio** transforms from **Oricorio** when given a Yellow Nectar.

Pa'u Oricorio.description: This Oricorio has sipped pink nectar. It gets so caught up in its dancing that it sometimes doesn’t hear its Trainer’s orders.
Pa'u Oricorio.evolution: **Pa'u Oricorio** transforms from **Oricorio** when given a Pink Nectar.

Sensu Oricorio.description: The elegant, attractive dance of these Oricorio is popular with adults, but the Oricorio themselves are hard to find in Paldea.
Sensu Oricorio.evolution: **Sensu Oricorio** transforms from **Oricorio** when given a Purple Nectar.

Cutiefly.description: An opponent’s aura can tell Cutiefly what that opponent’s next move will be. Then Cutiefly can glide around the attack and strike back.

Ribombee.description: Ribombee absolutely hate getting wet or rained on. In the cloudy Galar region, they are very seldom seen.

Rockruff.description: This Pokémon travels in a pack with others until it grows up. When its mood turns sour, it starts striking the ground with the rocks on its neck.
Rockruff.evolution: **Rockruff** evolves to **Lycanroc** starting from level 25 in the daytime, evolves to **Midnight Lycanroc** starting from level 25 in the nighttime and evolves to **Dusk Lycanroc** starting from level 25 in the dusktime.

Lycanroc.description: It has a calm and collected demeanor. It swiftly closes in on its prey, then slices them with the rocks in its mane.
Lycanroc.evolution: **Lycanroc** evolves from **Rockruff** starting from level 25 in the daytime.

Midnight Lycanroc.description: This Lycanroc has an extremely vicious temperament. It will happily sustain injuries for the sake of taking down its opponent.
Midnight Lycanroc.evolution: **Midnight Lycanroc** evolves from **Rockruff** starting from level 25 in the nighttime.

Dusk Lycanroc.description: These Pokémon have both calm and ferocious qualities. It’s said that this form of Lycanroc is the most troublesome to raise.
Dusk Lycanroc.evolution: **Dusk Lycanroc** evolves from **Rockruff** starting from level 25 in the dusktime.

Wishiwashi.description: When it senses danger, its eyes tear up. The sparkle of its tears signals other Wishiwashi to gather.
Wishiwashi.evolution: **Wishiwashi** transforms to **School Wishiwashi** starting from level 20.

School Wishiwashi.description: When facing tough opponents, they get into formation. But if they get wounded in battle, they’ll scatter and become solitary again.
School Wishiwashi.evolution: **School Wishiwashi** transforms from **Wishiwashi** starting from level 20.

Mareanie.description: It has excellent regenerative capabilities. Legs that a Mareanie has lost have a very bitter, astringent flavor—they’re not suitable as food.

Toxapex.description: Toxapex gets into fierce battles with Bruxish over areas where warm ocean currents flow, but the odds are always against it.

Mudbray.description: Though a slow walker, Mudbray is plenty strong. Its pace doesn’t change even when it’s loaded with 50 times its own body weight.

Mudsdale.description: Its legs are fortified with mud and harder than stone, and they can reduce a large truck to scrap with one kick.

Dewpider.description: Dewpider normally lives underwater. When it comes onto land in search of food, it takes water with it in the form of a bubble on its head.

Araquanid.description: It acts as a caretaker for Dewpider, putting them inside its bubble and letting them eat any leftover food.

Fomantis.description: Many Trainers give their Fomantis their own flowerpots so they can sunbathe in peace and quiet.
Fomantis.evolution: **Fomantis** evolves to **Lurantis** starting from level 34 in the daytime.

Lurantis.description: A lot of time and effort is required to maintain the vivid colors of its petals. This Pokémon puts its Trainer’s attentiveness to the test.
Lurantis.evolution: **Lurantis** evolves from **Fomantis** starting from level 34 in the daytime.

Morelull.description: Morelull live in forests that stay dark even during the day. They scatter flickering spores that put enemies to sleep.

Shiinotic.description: If you see a light deep in a forest at night, don’t go near. Shiinotic will make you fall fast asleep.

Salandit.description: Only female Salandit can produce gas laden with pheromones. Males entranced by this gas will do whatever the females tell them.
Salandit.evolution: **Salandit** evolves to **Salazzle** starting from level 33 as Female.

Salazzle.description: When two Salazzle meet, they will use their pheromone gas to fight over the males in each other’s group.
Salazzle.evolution: **Salazzle** evolves from **Salandit** starting from level 33 as Female.

Stufful.description: The way it protects itself by flailing its arms may be an adorable sight, but stay well away. This is flailing that can snap thick tree trunks.

Bewear.description: The moves it uses to take down its prey would make a martial artist jealous. It tucks subdued prey under its arms to carry them to its nest.

Bounsweet.description: A Greedent drawn in by the sweet scent of these Pokémon will tuck the Bounsweet in among the berries in its tail and carry them all away.
Bounsweet.evolution: **Bounsweet** evolves to **Steenee** starting from level 18, which evolves to **Tsareena** when leveled up while knowing Stomp.

Steenee.description: Steenee bounces energetically through forests. If the rind that peels off its body is pulverized, it can be used to treat stomach pains.
Steenee.evolution: **Steenee** evolves from **Bounsweet** starting from level 18 and evolves to **Tsareena** when leveled up while knowing Stomp.

Tsareena.description: This Pokémon launches fierce yet elegant kicks with its long, slender legs. It views Quaquaval as its rival.
Tsareena.evolution: **Tsareena** evolves from **Steenee** when leveled up while knowing Stomp, which evolves from **Bounsweet** starting from level 18.

Comfey.description: These Pokémon smell very nice. All Comfey wear different flowers, so each of these Pokémon has its own individual scent.

Oranguru.description: This Pokémon lives quietly in the depths of the forest. The purple, cape-like fur gets longer and longer as Oranguru ages.

Passimian.description: The boss chooses 10 members of the group to go out hunting. The hunting party will evenly split the food they find with the rest of the group.

Wimpod.description: Wimpod gather in swarms, constantly on the lookout for danger. They scatter the moment they detect an enemy’s presence.

Golisopod.description: They live in sunken ships or in holes in the seabed. When Golisopod and Grapploct battle, the loser becomes the winner’s meal.

Sandygast.description: It flings sand into the eyes of its prey and tries to close in on them while they’re blinded, but since Sandygast is so slow, the prey tends to escape.

Palossand.description: From the hollows in its arms, it fires the bones of its victims, which are all dried up after being drained of their vitality.
Palossand.evolution: Palossand evolves from Sandygast starting from level 42.

Pyukumuku.description: It’s covered in a slime that keeps its skin moist, allowing it to stay on land for days without drying up.

Type: Null.description: It was modeled after a mighty Pokémon of myth. The mask placed upon it limits its power in order to keep it under control.
Type: Null.evolution: **Type: Null** evolves to **Silvally** when leveled up while holding a Friendship Bracelet.

Silvally.description: The final factor needed to release this Pokémon’s true power was a strong bond with a Trainer it trusts.
Silvally.evolution: **Silvally** evolves from **Type: Null** when leveled up while holding a Friendship Bracelet.

Bug Silvally.description: The final factor needed to release this Pokémon’s true power was a strong bond with a Trainer it trusts.
Bug Silvally.evolution: **Bug Silvally** transforms from **Silvally** when given a Memory.

Dark Silvally.description: The final factor needed to release this Pokémon’s true power was a strong bond with a Trainer it trusts.
Dark Silvally.evolution: **Dark Silvally** transforms from **Silvally** when given a Memory.

Electric Silvally.evolution: **Electric Silvally** transforms from **Silvally** when given a Memory.

Fire Silvally.evolution: **Fire Silvally** transforms from **Silvally** when given a Memory.

Flying Silvally.evolution: **Flying Silvally** transforms from **Silvally** when given a Memory.

Ghost Silvally.evolution: **Ghost Silvally** transforms from **Silvally** when given a Memory.

Grass Silvally.evolution: **Grass Silvally** transforms from **Silvally** when given a Memory.
